ghs.en: Taichi: "Ahhh!!! So tireeed!!!"

ghs.en: Touko: "...thank you. For everything you've done for me."

rows.jp: 怒りのまま、冬子にクレームをつける。
rows.en: Still fuming, I let Touko have it.

ghs.en: Anger remains, so I file a complaint to Touko.
ghs.assessment: 怒りのまま says the narrator complains while still angry. 'Anger remains, so' turns the state into an explicit cause, while English files a complaint with or against someone rather than 'to' them.

highlights.text: Anger remains, so I file a complaint to Touko.

rows.jp: 「だいたいおまえは武道家のはしくれなんだから力仕事くらいできるだろうが！　カマトトぶりやがってもう底は見えてるんだよ！　すぺぺぺぺっ！」
rows.en: “You’re supposed to be some kind of martial artist! You could’ve done a little heavy lifting! Don’t pull that innocent-maiden act—I’ve already seen right through it! Pthththth!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Aren't you some leftover of a martial artist or something, you can do some physical labor too you know! I can see all through to the bottom of your feigned ignorance by the way! Ner-nernerner!"
ghs.assessment: 武道家のはしくれ means even a lowly or novice martial artist, not a leftover. カマトトぶる means to feign innocence, while 'some leftover of' and 'all through to the bottom' are not coherent English renderings.
ghs.remedy: Say that even a novice martial artist can handle physical work and that he sees through her feigned innocence.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Aren't you some leftover of a martial artist or something, you can do some physical labor too you know! I can see all through to the bottom of your feigned ignorance by the way! Ner-nernerner!"

rows.jp: 「……女の細腕に何させようってのよ。馬鹿じゃないの」
rows.en: “...And what exactly were you planning to make these frail feminine arms do? Idiot.”

ghs.en: Touko: "...what do you want a woman's thin arms to do! Aren't you stupid."
ghs.assessment: The English splices an exclamation onto 'what do you want ... to do' and then punctuates the following direct insult as a statement. The source contains two coherent challenges.
ghs.remedy: Use 'What are you trying to make these slender arms do? Are you stupid?'

highlights.text: Touko: "...what do you want a woman's thin arms to do! Aren't you stupid."

rows.jp: ちょっと気分を害した様子。

ghs.en: There was a little bit of offense in that.
ghs.assessment: The source observes that Tōko seems slightly offended. 'There was ... offense in that' turns her reaction into an abstract property of the prior speech.
ghs.remedy: Use 'She seems a little offended.'

highlights.text: There was a little bit of offense in that.

rows.jp: 冬子は雪だから優しくするとすぐトロトロとけるので、絶対甘い顔は見せないと決めた。
rows.en: Touko was made of winter snow: show her the slightest warmth and she melted. I resolved never to go soft on her.

ghs.en: Touko, written with the kanji for Winter and Child, is snow; therefore, when treated warmly she soon melts into a sticky syrupy mess. That is why she decided to absolutely never show her sweet side.
ghs.assessment: The narrator decides that he must never show Tōko indulgence because she melts when treated gently. The English makes Tōko the one who decides never to show her sweet side, reversing the acting subject and the lesson drawn from the snow metaphor.
ghs.remedy: Say that because Tōko melts when treated gently, the narrator resolves never to go easy on her.

highlights.text: Touko, written with the kanji for Winter and Child, is snow; therefore, when treated warmly she soon melts into a sticky syrupy mess. That is why she decided to absolutely never show her sweet side.

rows.en: “And what will you do, my dear? How can one helpless maiden hope to resist Mas Kurosu, living master of the Way of karade?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "If I do, what then? What opposition could a helpless young fujoshi of a woman, alone, pose? As an opponent of the 『Living Karadeka * 'The Trout' Kurosu』, even!"
ghs.assessment: 婦女子 means a woman or girl, not 腐女子, a fujoshi. The English imports the unrelated fandom label and leaves the mock-heroic challenge in broken prepositional syntax.
ghs.remedy: Use a grammatical challenge addressed to one helpless woman and preserve the narrator's mock title.

highlights.text: Taichi: "If I do, what then? What opposition could a helpless young fujoshi of a woman, alone, pose? As an opponent of the 『Living Karadeka * 'The Trout' Kurosu』, even!"

ghs.assessment: The source says the narrator asks Tōko in the manner of a perverted gentleman. 'So ask Touko with the tone of a gentlemen' has the wrong tense, lacks its subject, and mismatches singular 'a' with plural 'gentlemen.'
ghs.remedy: Use 'I ask Tōko in the tones of a gentlemanly pervert.'

highlights.text: So ask Touko with the tone of a gentlemen and a pervert.

rows.en: The blade clicked free of its scabbard.

ghs.en: The sound of the hilt of a sword being disconnected from the mouth of its scabbard.
ghs.assessment: 鯉口を切る is the practiced action of loosening a sword in its scabbard, producing a click. 'The mouth of its scabbard' literalizes the Japanese term and 'disconnected' describes the wrong mechanical relation.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I hear the click of a sword being loosened in its scabbard.'

highlights.text: The sound of the hilt of a sword being disconnected from the mouth of its scabbard.

ghs.en: Touko: "Slay."
ghs.assessment: 斬る is itself a clipped subject-and-object-less threat. Slay is ambiguous and unnatural in English, but the major omission rationale overstates what Japanese overtly supplies.
ghs.remedy: Use a concise natural cutting threat.

ghs.assessment: 段位なし means that she holds no rank. Leaving 'dan' untranslated obscures the joke for an English reader.

rows.en: “But the sword is excellent, so it cuts just fine!”

ghs.en: Touko: "But the sword is good and will cut you nicely!"
ghs.assessment: In the armed confrontation the listener is the obvious prospective object, licensing will cut you. Only the incongruous nicely remains unsupported.
ghs.remedy: Remove nicely and keep the threat.

highlights.text: Touko: "But the sword is good and will cut you nicely!"

rows.jp: 「居合いの理念に反するんじゃないのかそれは！」
rows.en: “Doesn’t that violate the entire philosophy of iaido?!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Isn't what you just did against the philosophy of unsheathe-cut-sheathe of the Iai!"
ghs.assessment: The line asks whether her behavior violates the philosophy of iai. 'The philosophy of unsheathe-cut-sheathe of the Iai' is not grammatical English and replaces the discipline with an improvised procedure label.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Doesn't that violate the philosophy of iai?'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Isn't what you just did against the philosophy of unsheathe-cut-sheathe of the Iai!"

rows.jp: 居合とは、人に斬られず人斬らず、己を責めて平らかの道……。
rows.en: Iaido: be cut by none, cut down no one; hold yourself to account and walk the path of peace...

ghs.en: Iai is a peaceful way of self-criticism where no man is slain and is slain by no man...
ghs.assessment: 己を責めて describes disciplining or mastering oneself on a peaceful path. 'Self-criticism' reduces it to fault-finding, while the doubled passive obscures the balanced injunction neither to cut nor be cut.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Iai is a peaceful path: cut no one, be cut by no one, and discipline the self.'

highlights.text: Iai is a peaceful way of self-criticism where no man is slain and is slain by no man...

rows.jp: 「生き恥をかくぐらいならば、いっそもろとも！」
rows.en: “Better we both perish than I endure a life of shame!”

ghs.en: Touko: "If a life of disgrace is what awaits, then this is better for all of us!"
ghs.assessment: いっそもろとも threatens to take both of them down together rather than live in disgrace. 'This is better for all of us' turns mutual destruction into a beneficial collective outcome.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Rather than live in disgrace, I'll take us both down!'

highlights.text: Touko: "If a life of disgrace is what awaits, then this is better for all of us!"

ghs.en: Taichi: "UEITSU! UEITSU!"
ghs.assessment: ウエイツ is the deliberately Japanized sound of the English plea 'Wait,' leading into the narrator's temporary-American joke. 'UEITSU' merely retransliterates the katakana and leaves the plea unintelligible.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Wait! Wait!'

highlights.text: Taichi: "UEITSU! UEITSU!"

rows.jp: 俺は一時の米国人と化して諫めた。

ghs.assessment: しまってくれ asks her to put the dangerous sword away. 'Drop the danger on your side' instead suggests discarding an abstract danger and does not express sheathing or stowing the weapon.
ghs.remedy: Use a faux-American but intelligible request for her to put the dangerous thing away.

highlights.text: Taichi: "And now you shall repent. In the world of 451 Fahrenheit, where books spontaneously combust! In other words you are to be condemned into the fires of hell! That is the reward for roasting books of learning! You damn enemy of mankind!"

rows.en: With both hands, I seized the half-escaped thing and hauled it back in like a fisherman pulling up a dragnet.

ghs.en: Making my hands as if a net, I haul in the escaping 'thing'.
ghs.assessment: The narrator uses both hands to haul the escaping thing back like pulling in a beach seine. 'Making my hands as if a net' is not grammatical and turns the hauling simile into a claim that his hands become the net.
ghs.remedy: Use 'With both hands, I haul the escaping thing back in as though pulling in a beach seine.'

Taichi: "Re * suscitation!"
ghs.assessment: 復活 is the emphatic declaration 'Revival!' or 'Back to life!' 'Suscitation' is not the intended English word, and splitting it as 'Re * suscitation' makes the cry unintelligible.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Re-viv-al!'
